components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.
马 (horse) — horses: 骑, 驾, 骄; 验 first meant testing a horse, then any test.
佥 (qiān) gives the -ian rhyme; same part in 险 xiǎn, 检 jiǎn, 脸 liǎn, 签 qiān.

example.hanzi: 学生们在实验室做化学实验。
example.pinyin: Xuéshengmen zài shíyànshì zuò huàxué shíyàn.
example.english: The students are doing a chemistry experiment in the lab.
example.fact: 验 (马 "horse" + phonetic 佥) originally meant examining or testing a horse before a purchase or a long journey — its sense broadened over the centuries from that literal check-up into the general "to test, to verify" that it carries in 实验 today.

examples.hanzi: 这个实验需要做三次。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shíyàn xūyào zuò sān cì.
examples.english: This experiment needs to be done three times.

examples.hanzi: 科学家们用小白鼠做实验。
examples.pinyin: Kēxuéjiāmen yòng xiǎo báishǔ zuò shíyàn.
examples.english: Scientists run experiments with white mice.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — words and talk: 说, 话, 读; a spoken mistake or misunderstanding.
吴 (wú) gives the sound (wù, tone differs); same series 娱 yú and 虞 yú.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 对不起,这只是一个误会。
example.pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, zhè zhǐshì yí gè wùhuì.
example.english: Sorry, this is just a misunderstanding.
example.fact: 误 (讠 "speech" + phonetic 吴) originally named an error made specifically in speaking, only later broadening to cover any kind of mistake — the sense it carries when paired with 会 ("to understand") in 误会.

examples.hanzi: 你误会我了,我没有那个意思。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ wùhuì wǒ le, wǒ méiyǒu nàge yìsi.
examples.english: You've misunderstood me, I didn't mean that.

examples.hanzi: 他们之间有一点儿误会,解释一下就好了。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zhījiān yǒu yìdiǎnr wùhuì, jiěshì yíxià jiù hǎo le.
examples.english: There's a small misunderstanding between them that an explanation will fix.

components.note: 户 (door) — 户 is a door with 口 below — 启 is opening; the traditional 啓 added a hand.
力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.

example.hanzi: 请按这个按钮启动电脑。
example.pinyin: Qǐng àn zhège ànniǔ qǐdòng diànnǎo.
example.english: Please press this button to start the computer.
example.fact: 启 pictures a door (户) swinging open (口) — 启动 extends that literal image of "opening up" into the abstract sense of setting a machine, process, or plan into motion.

examples.hanzi: 我的手机启动得很慢。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī qǐdòng de hěn màn.
examples.english: My phone starts up very slowly.

examples.hanzi: 公司下个月将启动新的项目。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī xià ge yuè jiāng qǐdòng xīn de xiàngmù.
examples.english: The company will launch a new project next month.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 爱; 恋 is to love or long for.
The sound part is traditional 戀 (luán), replaced in 恋 by 亦 (yì) only for simplicity — a loose clue for liàn.
友 (friend) replaces the heart-and-foot lower part of the traditional 愛, which had 心 (heart); so 爱 lost its heart in simplification.

example.hanzi: 他们谈恋爱三年了,准备结婚。
example.pinyin: Tāmen tán liàn'ài sān nián le, zhǔnbèi jiéhūn.
example.english: They've been dating for three years and are getting ready to get married.
example.fact: 恋爱 is almost always paired with the verb 谈 ("to talk, to carry on") in the fixed phrase 谈恋爱, literally "to converse a romance" — a reminder that 恋爱 behaves more like a noun object than a stand-alone verb in everyday speech.

examples.hanzi: 他们俩在大学时开始恋爱。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen liǎ zài dàxué shí kāishǐ liàn'ài.
examples.english: The two of them started dating in college.

examples.hanzi: 我现在不想恋爱,想先把工作做好。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài bù xiǎng liàn'ài, xiǎng xiān bǎ gōngzuò zuòhǎo.
examples.english: I don't want to date now, I want to do well at work first.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 哟 is an interjection.
约 (yuē) — loose sound hint (yō vs yuē).

example.hanzi: 哟,你今天穿得真漂亮!
example.pinyin: Yō, nǐ jīntiān chuān de zhēn piàoliang!
example.english: Oh, you look really pretty today!
example.fact: 哟 expresses mild surprise, often with a teasing or admiring edge. At the end of a sentence it can soften the tone as a light particle (neutral tone yo), as in songs and lively speech: 加油哟 (come on!).

examples.hanzi: 哟，你来得真早！
examples.pinyin: Yō, nǐ láide zhēn zǎo!
examples.english: Oh, you're here really early!

examples.hanzi: 哟，下雪了！
examples.pinyin: Yō, xiàxuě le!
examples.english: Oh, it's snowing!

components.note: 廴 (long stride) — a rare radical of walking and extending, also in 延 yán and 廷 tíng; 建 means to set up or put up; the sound clue 聿 is only loose.

example.hanzi: 他们在河边建了一座桥。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài hé biān jiàn le yí zuò qiáo.
example.english: They built a bridge by the river.
example.fact: 建 suits large or formal constructions and institutions: 建国 (found a country), 建立 (establish), 建筑 (architecture). It also gives 建议, 'suggestion'. For an ordinary house, speakers often use 盖 (gài) instead.

examples.hanzi: 他们要在这里建一所学校。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen yào zài zhèlǐ jiàn yì suǒ xuéxiào.
examples.english: They are going to build a school here.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市是一千年前建的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì shì yì qiān nián qián jiàn de.
examples.english: This city was built a thousand years ago.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 住; 候 means to wait for someone.
侯 (hóu) is a close sound clue for hòu; it also gives 猴 hóu monkey and 喉 hóu throat.

example.hanzi: 小时候,我最喜欢在河边玩耍。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo shíhou, wǒ zuì xǐhuan zài hébiān wánshuǎ.
example.english: When I was little, I loved playing by the river.
example.fact: 小时候 tucks 时候 ("time, moment") behind 小 ("small, young") to mean literally "the small-time," i.e. one's early years — it works as a fixed time expression that typically opens a sentence, much like English "back then" or "as a kid."

examples.hanzi: 小时候,我家养过一只小狗。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoshíhou, wǒ jiā yǎng guo yì zhī xiǎo gǒu.
examples.english: When I was little, my family had a puppy.

examples.hanzi: 他小时候很怕黑。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎoshíhou hěn pà hēi.
examples.english: He was afraid of the dark as a child.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.
页 (head, page) — heads and faces, as in 头 head, 顶 top, 额 forehead; 题 first meant forehead, then "heading".
是 (shì) gives a loose sound clue for tí; 是 also sounds out 提 tí and 堤 dī.

example.hanzi: 这个话题我们已经讨论过很多次了。
example.pinyin: Zhège huàtí wǒmen yǐjīng tǎolùn guò hěn duō cì le.
example.english: We've already discussed this topic many times.
example.fact: 话题 combines 话 ("speech, words") with 题, itself built from 页 ("head") for the "heading" placed at the top of a piece of writing — so 话题 pictures a conversation's own heading, the subject printed at the top of what's being said.

examples.hanzi: 我们换个话题吧,聊点轻松的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen huàn ge huàtí ba, liáo diǎn qīngsōng de.
examples.english: Let's change the subject and talk about something lighter.

examples.hanzi: 天气是人们最常聊的话题。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì shì rénmen zuì cháng liáo de huàtí.
examples.english: The weather is the topic people talk about most.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth family: 布, 带, 帽. Memory aid: a market stall with a cloth banner 巾 under a roof 亠, i.e. a 市 market.
柿 (shì, persimmon) — contains 市 as a sound part, same sound shì.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.

example.hanzi: 这种新产品在市场上很受欢迎。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng xīn chǎnpǐn zài shìchǎng shàng hěn shòu huānyíng.
example.english: This new product is very popular in the market.
example.fact: 场 (土 "earth" + phonetic 昜) originally named any flattened open ground used for a specific activity, like a threshing floor or drill ground — 市场 narrows that general "activity ground" down to the ground specifically used for buying and selling.

examples.hanzi: 周末我们去农贸市场买菜。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù nóngmào shìchǎng mǎi cài.
examples.english: On weekends we go to the farmers' market to buy vegetables.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司想进入中国市场。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī xiǎng jìnrù Zhōngguó shìchǎng.
examples.english: This company wants to enter the Chinese market.

components.note: 木 (tree) — marks trees and wooden things, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; 栋 is the main beam of a house, now a measure word for buildings.
东 (dōng) — close sound: 栋 dòng. 东 also sounds out 冻 dòng and 动 dòng.

example.hanzi: 那栋楼有三十层。
example.pinyin: Nà dòng lóu yǒu sānshí céng.
example.english: That building has thirty floors.
example.fact: 栋 is the measure word for buildings: 一栋楼, 一栋房子. Its original meaning is the ridgepole, the main beam of a roof, which is why it counts whole buildings. 幢 (zhuàng) is a close alternative for the same job.

examples.hanzi: 我家住在三号楼的那栋房子里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā zhù zài sān hào lóu de nà dòng fángzi lǐ.
examples.english: My family lives in that house in Building 3.

examples.hanzi: 学校新建了一栋教学楼。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào xīn jiàn le yí dòng jiàoxuélóu.
examples.english: The school has built a new teaching building.

components.note: 木 — a tree with trunk, branches and roots; the wood radical, as in 林 forest, 树 tree, 桌 table.

example.hanzi: 这张桌子是木头做的。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi shì mùtou zuò de.
example.english: This table is made of wood.
example.fact: 木 is the 'wood' element in the Five Elements (五行: metal, wood, water, fire, earth). It rarely stands alone: 木头 (wood), 树木 (trees), 木材 (timber). It can also mean numb, as in 麻木.

examples.hanzi: 我家的地板是木地板。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā de dìbǎn shì mù dìbǎn.
examples.english: Our floor is a wooden floor.

examples.hanzi: 院子里种了几棵树木。
examples.pinyin: Yuànzi li zhòng le jǐ kē shùmù.
examples.english: A few trees were planted in the yard.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国, 园, 围; 团 is a round group. Its traditional form had 專 as sound, like 转 zhuǎn and 传 chuán.

example.hanzi: 我们跟旅行团去了日本。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen gēn lǚxíngtuán qù le Rìběn.
example.english: We went to Japan with a tour group.
example.fact: 团 means both 'round ball' and 'group': 饭团 (rice ball), 旅行团 (tour group), 团队 (team). 团圆 means a family reunion, and the 团圆饭 is the New Year's Eve dinner. It is the simplified form of 團.

examples.hanzi: 学校有一个学生合唱团。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào yǒu yí ge xuésheng héchàngtuán.
examples.english: The school has a student choir.

examples.hanzi: 过年的时候,大家团聚在一起。
examples.pinyin: Guònián de shíhou, dàjiā tuánjù zài yìqǐ.
examples.english: At New Year, everyone gets together.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 线; 练 first meant boiling silk to soften it, then practice.
柬 (jiǎn) is a loose sound clue; same part in 炼 liàn and 简 jiǎn.

example.hanzi: 我每天练习写汉字。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān liànxí xiě Hànzì.
example.english: I practice writing Chinese characters every day.
example.fact: 练 is for building skills through repetition: 练习 (practice), 训练 (training), 练字 (practice calligraphy). Do not mix it up with 炼 (liàn, to smelt or refine), which sounds the same; 锻炼 'exercise' uses that one.

examples.hanzi: 你的汉字写得不错,多练练就更好了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de Hànzì xiě de búcuò, duō liànliàn jiù gèng hǎo le.
examples.english: Your characters are good; a bit more practice and they'll be even better.

examples.hanzi: 他每周去健身房练三次。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi zhōu qù jiànshēnfáng liàn sān cì.
examples.english: He works out at the gym three times a week.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 迷 is losing one's way.
米 (mǐ) — near sound — 迷 is mí, the same syllable with a different tone.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 桂林的风景非常迷人。
example.pinyin: Guìlín de fēngjǐng fēicháng mírén.
example.english: Guilin's scenery is extremely enchanting.
example.fact: 迷 (辶 "to walk" + phonetic 米) originally described losing one's way while walking — 迷人 literally means "person-losing," something so captivating it makes you lose your bearings, the same root behind 迷路 ("to get lost") and 迷恋 ("to be infatuated with").

examples.hanzi: 她的笑容非常迷人。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xiàoróng fēicháng mírén.
examples.english: Her smile is very charming.

examples.hanzi: 夜晚的海边安静又迷人。
examples.pinyin: Yèwǎn de hǎibiān ānjìng yòu mírén.
examples.english: The seaside at night is quiet and enchanting.

components.note: 力 (strength) — with 口 mouth: adding strength by words, hence to add, to increase. 加 also in 架 jià and 驾 jià.
州 (region) — a river 川 with small islands of land in it; 州 is a region, and also sounds out 洲 zhōu.

example.hanzi: 我的表姐住在加州的洛杉矶。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de biǎojiě zhù zài Jiāzhōu de Luòshānjī.
example.english: My cousin lives in Los Angeles, California.
example.fact: 加州 shortens the full transliteration 加利福尼亚州 down to just its first and last syllables — 加 (borrowed purely for its sound) plus 州 ("state, province") — the same clipping pattern behind other US state nicknames, like 德州 for Texas (德克萨斯州).

examples.hanzi: 加州的天气一年四季都很好。
examples.pinyin: Jiāzhōu de tiānqì yì nián sìjì dōu hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The weather in California is nice all year round.

examples.hanzi: 他大学毕业后搬去了加州工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā dàxué bìyè hòu bān qù le Jiāzhōu gōngzuò.
examples.english: After graduating, he moved to California for work.

components.note: 木 (tree) — marks trees and wooden things, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; 桥 is a bridge, once of wood.
乔 (qiáo) — same sound: 桥 qiáo. 乔 also sounds out 轿 jiào and 骄 jiāo.

example.hanzi: 这座桥有一百年了。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo yǒu yìbǎi nián le.
example.english: This bridge is a hundred years old.
example.fact: Bridges take the measure word 座 (一座桥). The idiom 过河拆桥, 'tear down the bridge after crossing the river', describes someone who abandons the people who helped them. 桥 also names the card game bridge: 桥牌.

examples.hanzi: 河上有一座古老的桥。
examples.pinyin: Hé shang yǒu yí zuò gǔlǎo de qiáo.
examples.english: There is an old bridge over the river.

examples.hanzi: 过了这座桥,马上就到了。
examples.pinyin: Guò le zhè zuò qiáo, mǎshàng jiù dào le.
examples.english: Once you cross this bridge, you're almost there.

components.note: 廴 (long stride) — a rare radical of walking and extending, also in 延 yán and 廷 tíng; 建 means to set up or put up; the sound clue 聿 is only loose.
⺮ (bamboo) — ⺮ is bamboo, as in 笔, 筷, 箱; 筑 was an old instrument, and 建筑 is building, from the older form 築.

example.hanzi: 这座建筑有两百年的历史了。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò jiànzhù yǒu liǎng bǎi nián de lìshǐ le.
example.english: This building has a two-hundred-year history.
example.fact: 筑 pairs the bamboo radical ⺮ with 巩 ("firm, secure") — early construction work often relied on bamboo scaffolding and poles, so the character still carries a trace of that original building material even though 建筑 today covers structures made of anything.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市有很多有名的现代建筑。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì yǒu hěn duō yǒumíng de xiàndài jiànzhù.
examples.english: This city has many famous modern buildings.

examples.hanzi: 他们打算在河边建筑一座新桥。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen dǎsuàn zài hébiān jiànzhù yí zuò xīn qiáo.
examples.english: They plan to build a new bridge by the river.

components.note: 手 (hand) — the bottom 手 is a hand — 举 is lifting with the hands, as in 举行.
彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.

example.hanzi: 婚礼将在下周六举行。
example.pinyin: Hūnlǐ jiāng zài xià zhōu liù jǔxíng.
example.english: The wedding will be held next Saturday.
example.fact: 举行 is reserved for formal, scheduled events — ceremonies, meetings, competitions — and sounds odd applied to a casual get-together, where Chinese instead reaches for simpler verbs like 开 ("to hold/start [a meeting]").

examples.hanzi: 今年的运动会将在十月举行。
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián de yùndònghuì jiāng zài shí yuè jǔxíng.
examples.english: This year's sports meet will be held in October.

examples.hanzi: 公司明天上午举行新产品发布会。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī míngtiān shàngwǔ jǔxíng xīn chǎnpǐn fābùhuì.
examples.english: The company is holding a new product launch tomorrow morning.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 损 is to damage, as in 损失.
员 (yuán) — loose hint — 损 is sǔn.
夫 (man) — the main part. Dictionary reading: something 丿 slipping from a hand. Memory aid: a man 夫 dropping what he held — 失去 to lose.

example.hanzi: 这场火灾造成了巨大的损失。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng huǒzāi zàochéng le jùdà de sǔnshī.
example.english: This fire caused enormous losses.
example.fact: 损失 works as both a noun ("a loss") and a verb ("to lose, to suffer damage") without changing form at all — a common trait of two-character Chinese compounds that English usually has to render with two separate words.

examples.hanzi: 这次失败给公司带来了很大的损失。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì shībài gěi gōngsī dàilái le hěn dà de sǔnshī.
examples.english: This failure caused the company a big loss.

examples.hanzi: 你不用担心,这点小损失不算什么。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bú yòng dānxīn, zhè diǎn xiǎo sǔnshī bú suàn shénme.
examples.english: Don't worry, this small loss is nothing.

components.note: 王 (king) — three bars for heaven, people and earth joined by a vertical: the ruler who links them. As 玉 jade with its dot dropped it also marks jewels: 球, 玩.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 那个王子最后娶了灰姑娘。
example.pinyin: Nàge wángzǐ zuìhòu qǔ le Huīgūniang.
example.english: In the end, the prince married Cinderella.
example.fact: 王子 builds directly on its two parts — 王 ("king") plus 子 ("son") — literally "king's son," one of the more transparent titles in the royal vocabulary, alongside 公主 ("princess").

examples.hanzi: 王子和公主最后幸福地生活在一起。
examples.pinyin: Wángzǐ hé gōngzhǔ zuìhòu xìngfú de shēnghuó zài yìqǐ.
examples.english: The prince and the princess lived happily together in the end.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事讲的是一位年轻的王子。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi jiǎng de shì yí wèi niánqīng de wángzǐ.
examples.english: This story is about a young prince.

components.note: 石 (stone) — stones and minerals: 破, 研, 砖; 码 first meant stone weights, then numbers.
马 (mǎ) sounds exactly like 码; also in 吗, 骂 mà, 妈 mā.

example.hanzi: 请告诉我你的手机号码。
example.pinyin: Qǐng gàosu wǒ nǐ de shǒujī hàomǎ.
example.english: Please tell me your phone number.
example.fact: 码 is behind many words for numbers and codes: 号码 (number), 密码 (password), 二维码 (QR code), 代码 (source code) and 尺码 (clothing size). It is also the unit 'yard' in measurements.

examples.hanzi: 这双运动鞋是几码的?
examples.pinyin: Zhè shuāng yùndòngxié shì jǐ mǎ de?
examples.english: What size are these sneakers?

examples.hanzi: 请扫一下这个二维码。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng sǎo yíxià zhège èrwéimǎ.
examples.english: Please scan this QR code.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 退 is to step back.
后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).

example.hanzi: 消防员让围观的人都退后一点。
example.pinyin: Xiāofángyuán ràng wéiguān de rén dōu tuìhòu yìdiǎn.
example.english: The firefighter told the onlookers to all step back a little.
example.fact: 退 already means "to retreat, to move backward" on its own (辶 "to walk" + phonetic 艮), and 后 means "behind, back" — 退后 reinforces the same backward direction twice, the same near-synonym doubling strategy behind words like 喜欢 and 应该.

examples.hanzi: 前面有危险,请大家退后。
examples.pinyin: Qiánmiàn yǒu wēixiǎn, qǐng dàjiā tuìhòu.
examples.english: There is danger ahead, everyone please stand back.

examples.hanzi: 他害怕地退后了两步。
examples.pinyin: Tā hàipà de tuìhòu le liǎng bù.
examples.english: He took two steps back in fear.

components.note: 丹 (cinnabar) — an ancient picture of a mine with cinnabar in it; 丹 is red, as in 牡丹.

example.hanzi: 古人相信吃丹药可以长生不老。
example.pinyin: Gǔrén xiāngxìn chī dānyào kěyǐ chángshēng bùlǎo.
example.english: People in ancient times believed that taking elixir pills could grant immortality.
example.fact: 丹 was originally cinnabar, a red mineral. Daoist alchemists made 丹药 (elixirs) from it in the hope of immortality, and 丹田 names the energy center below the navel. It also appears in 牡丹 (peony) and 丹麦 (Denmark).

examples.hanzi: 牡丹是洛阳有名的花。
examples.pinyin: Mǔdān shì Luòyáng yǒumíng de huā.
examples.english: The peony is a famous flower of Luoyang.

examples.hanzi: 我的朋友来自丹麦。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de péngyou láizì Dānmài.
examples.english: My friend comes from Denmark.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
豕 (pig) — 豕 is a pig, as in 象; 豪 was a bristly boar, then a hero; 高 gives the near sound (also in 毫 háo).

example.hanzi: 父母为孩子的成绩感到很自豪。
example.pinyin: Fùmǔ wèi háizi de chéngjì gǎndào hěn zìháo.
example.english: The parents feel very proud of their child's achievements.
example.fact: 豪 depicts a bristling wild boar (豕) with the phonetic 高 layered above — its older sense of a fierce, formidable creature broadened into "heroic, grand," the same bold flavor 自豪 keeps: not mere satisfaction, but a robust pride in one's own accomplishment.

examples.hanzi: 我为我的国家感到自豪。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ wèi wǒ de guójiā gǎndào zìháo.
examples.english: I feel proud of my country.

examples.hanzi: 他自豪地给大家看了自己的作品。
examples.pinyin: Tā zìháo de gěi dàjiā kàn le zìjǐ de zuòpǐn.
examples.english: He proudly showed everyone his work.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脸, 脑); 肚 is the belly.
土 (tǔ) — near sound — 肚 is dù; 土 also sounds out 吐 tǔ.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 我肚子饿了,想去吃饭。
example.pinyin: Wǒ dùzi è le, xiǎng qù chīfàn.
example.english: My stomach is growling, I want to go eat.
example.fact: 肚子 is the everyday, colloquial word for the stomach or belly — the more formal, technical word for the internal organ is 胃 (wèi), reserved mainly for medical contexts.

examples.hanzi: 我吃得太多,肚子有点儿疼。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chī de tài duō, dùzi yǒudiǎnr téng.
examples.english: I ate too much and my stomach hurts a bit.

examples.hanzi: 她的肚子圆圆的,里面有个小宝宝。
examples.pinyin: Tā de dùzi yuányuán de, lǐmiàn yǒu ge xiǎo bǎobao.
examples.english: Her belly is round, with a little baby inside.

meanings: to expel (a member of an organization)

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
阝 on the left is 阜 (steps, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: 除 first meant palace steps; to step away, remove.
余 (yú) is a loose sound clue for chú; 余 also in 涂 tú, 途 tú and 徐 xú.

example.hanzi: 他因为旷工太多被公司开除了。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi kuànggōng tài duō bèi gōngsī kāichú le.
example.english: He was fired by the company for missing too much work.
example.fact: 开除 carries a formal, disciplinary tone — used for expelling a student or firing an employee specifically for wrongdoing — distinct from the more neutral 辞退 or 解雇 ("to lay off"), which don't necessarily imply punishment.

examples.hanzi: 他因为工作不认真被公司开除了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi gōngzuò bú rènzhēn bèi gōngsī kāichú le.
examples.english: He was fired by the company for not working carefully.

examples.hanzi: 这个学生被学校开除了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xuésheng bèi xuéxiào kāichú le.
examples.english: This student was expelled from the school.

meanings: (as a correlative conjunction) not only (..., but also ...)

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
亻 (person) — person radical; 仅 is the simplified form of 僅.
又 (yòu) — in the old form 僅 the sound came from 堇 (jǐn); 仅 and 谨 jǐn sound the same.

example.hanzi: 她不仅会说英语,还会说法语。
example.pinyin: Tā bùjǐn huì shuō Yīngyǔ, hái huì shuō Fǎyǔ.
example.english: She can not only speak English, but also French.
example.fact: 不仅 almost always sets up a paired construction with 还 or 而且 ("but also") later in the sentence — the same "not only...but also" template English uses, making it one of the more directly transferable conjunctions for English speakers.

examples.hanzi: 这个方法不仅简单,而且很有效。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fāngfǎ bù jǐn jiǎndān, érqiě hěn yǒuxiào.
examples.english: This method is not only simple, but also effective.

examples.hanzi: 不仅孩子们喜欢,大人们也很喜欢。
examples.pinyin: Bù jǐn háizimen xǐhuan, dàrénmen yě hěn xǐhuan.
examples.english: Not only do the children like it, the adults do too.

components.note: 自 (self/nose) — the middle part, as in 臭 smell; it does not explain 'summer'. Memory aid: your own nose feeling the heat.
夂 (go slowly) — the bottom part and radical, a foot. The old form shows a figure in ceremonial dress; as a memory aid only.
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.hanzi: 夏天的时候,这里非常热。
example.pinyin: Xiàtiān de shíhou, zhèlǐ fēicháng rè.
example.english: In the summer, it's extremely hot here.
example.fact: All four Mandarin season words follow the same "[season] + 天" pattern — 春天, 夏天, 秋天, 冬天 — with 天 (literally "sky, day") functioning as a generic time-of-year suffix rather than meaning a literal single day.

examples.hanzi: 夏天我们常常去海边游泳。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān wǒmen chángcháng qù hǎibiān yóuyǒng.
examples.english: In summer, we often go swimming at the beach.

examples.hanzi: 今年夏天特别热,每天都有三十五度。
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián xiàtiān tèbié rè, měi tiān dōu yǒu sānshíwǔ dù.
examples.english: This summer is especially hot, with thirty-five degrees every day.

components.note: 饣 (food) — 饣 is the simplified 食 (food), as in 饭, 饺, 饿; 饼 is a flat baked cake.
并 (bìng) — near sound — 饼 is bǐng; 并 also sounds out 拼 pīn.
干 (dry; do) — a forked pole or shield. It lends its sound to 肝 gān, 杆 gān, 赶 gǎn, 汗 hàn and 岸 àn.

example.hanzi: 妈妈烤了一些巧克力饼干。
example.pinyin: Māma kǎo le yìxiē qiǎokèlì bǐnggān.
example.english: Mom baked some chocolate cookies.
example.fact: 饼 names any flat, round cake-like food — the same root appears in 月饼 ("mooncake") and 馅饼 ("a filled pastry") — while 干, read here as gān rather than its more common reading gàn ("to do"), keeps its older sense "dry," describing the biscuit's crisp texture.

examples.hanzi: 我喝茶的时候喜欢吃几块饼干。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hē chá de shíhou xǐhuan chī jǐ kuài bǐnggān.
examples.english: I like to eat a few cookies when I drink tea.

examples.hanzi: 这盒饼干是奶奶寄给我的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè hé bǐnggān shì nǎinai jì gěi wǒ de.
examples.english: This box of biscuits was sent to me by Grandma.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: to prove by saying.
正 (zhèng) gives the exact sound; 正 also in 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 请出示你的身份证。
example.pinyin: Qǐng chūshì nǐ de shēnfènzhèng.
example.english: Please show your ID card.
example.fact: 证 is the word on many documents: 身份证 (ID card), 学生证 (student card), 证件 (documents) and 证明 (to prove). Note the homophones 证, 症 (symptom) and 政 (politics); context and the radical tell them apart.

examples.hanzi: 办签证需要带护照。
examples.pinyin: Bàn qiānzhèng xūyào dài hùzhào.
examples.english: You need to bring your passport to apply for a visa.

examples.hanzi: 他拿出证据来证明自己没错。
examples.pinyin: Tā ná chū zhèngjù lái zhèngmíng zìjǐ méi cuò.
examples.english: He produced evidence to prove he was not wrong.

components.note: 母 (mother) — a woman 女 with two dots for breasts: a nursing mother. 母 also appears in 每 měi, 海 hǎi and 梅 méi.

example.hanzi: 我的母亲是老师。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de mǔqīn shì lǎoshī.
example.english: My mother is a teacher.
example.fact: 母亲 is the formal word for mother, while 妈妈 is the everyday one. 母 also marks females of animals (母鸡, hen) and appears in 母语 (native language) and 母校 (one's alma mater).

examples.hanzi: 母亲节我给妈妈买了花。
examples.pinyin: Mǔqīnjié wǒ gěi māma mǎi le huā.
examples.english: On Mother's Day I bought flowers for my mom.

examples.hanzi: 这只母鸡每天下一个蛋。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī mǔ jī měitiān xià yí ge dàn.
examples.english: This hen lays one egg every day.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
夭 (yāo) is a loose sound clue for xiào; 夭 also in 妖 yāo. The bamboo top ⺮ here is a historical shape, not a meaning clue.

example.hanzi: 他的借口听起来很可笑。
example.pinyin: Tā de jièkǒu tīng qǐlai hěn kěxiào.
example.english: His excuse sounds very ridiculous.
example.fact: 可笑 leans toward the mocking end of "funny," closer to "ridiculous, laughable," while its near-twin 好笑 stays neutral or even affectionate, closer to plain "funny" — a distinction worth knowing before calling something 可笑 to someone's face.

examples.hanzi: 他穿着一条很可笑的裤子。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuān zhe yì tiáo hěn kěxiào de kùzi.
examples.english: He is wearing a pair of ridiculous pants.

examples.hanzi: 你这个想法真可笑,根本做不到。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhège xiǎngfǎ zhēn kěxiào, gēnběn zuò bú dào.
examples.english: This idea of yours is laughable, it can't be done at all.

components.note: 来 (come, wheat) — traditional 麥 combined 來 (the old word for the wheat plant) with a foot 夂 — a grain brought in; 麦 is the wheat radical.

example.hanzi: 这里种了很多小麦。
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ zhòng le hěn duō xiǎomài.
example.english: A lot of wheat is grown here.
example.fact: 麦 is the grain: 小麦 (wheat), 大麦 (barley), 麦子, 麦片 (oatmeal). Many scholars note that 来 (come) began as a drawing of a wheat plant, so the 'come' and 'wheat' characters are old relatives. Be careful not to mix up 麦 mài, 买 mǎi and 卖 mài.

examples.hanzi: 他早餐喜欢吃麦片。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǎocān xǐhuan chī màipiàn.
examples.english: He likes to eat oatmeal for breakfast.

examples.hanzi: 我们去麦当劳吃汉堡吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen qù Màidāngláo chī hànbǎo ba.
examples.english: Let's go to McDonald's for a burger.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 灬 is fire at the bottom, as in 点, 照, 熟; 热 is heat.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.

example.hanzi: 服务员对客人非常热情。
example.pinyin: Fúwùyuán duì kèrén fēicháng rèqíng.
example.english: The waiter is extremely warm and friendly toward guests.
example.fact: 热情 covers ground English splits into several separate words — "warmth," "enthusiasm," "hospitality," "passion" — all folded into one word equally at home describing a friendly host, an eager volunteer, or a passionate romance.

examples.hanzi: 他对每一位顾客都很热情。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì měi yí wèi gùkè dōu hěn rèqíng.
examples.english: He is warm to every customer.

examples.hanzi: 她对做饭的热情一直没变。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zuòfàn de rèqíng yìzhí méi biàn.
examples.english: Her passion for cooking has never changed.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: to prove by saying.
正 (zhèng) gives the exact sound; 正 also in 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 他愿意在法庭上为朋友作证。
example.pinyin: Tā yuànyì zài fǎtíng shàng wèi péngyou zuòzhèng.
example.english: He is willing to testify in court for his friend.
example.fact: 证 (讠 "speech" + 正 "straight, correct") literally means speaking the straight truth — 作证, "to make/do 证," turns that noun for "proof, evidence" into the everyday verb "to testify," the same 作 + [noun] pattern that forms 作案 ("to commit a crime").

examples.hanzi: 他的邻居愿意为他作证。
examples.pinyin: Tā de línjū yuànyì wèi tā zuòzhèng.
examples.english: His neighbor is willing to testify for him.

examples.hanzi: 你能为我作证吗?当时你也在场。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng wèi wǒ zuòzhèng ma? Dāngshí nǐ yě zàichǎng.
examples.english: Can you vouch for me? You were there too.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
夭 (yāo) is a loose sound clue for xiào; 夭 also in 妖 yāo. The bamboo top ⺮ here is a historical shape, not a meaning clue.

example.hanzi: 这个笑话真好笑!
example.pinyin: Zhège xiàohua zhēn hǎoxiào!
example.english: This joke is really funny!
example.fact: 好笑 is built the same way as 好吃 ("delicious," literally "good to eat") and 好看 ("good-looking," literally "good to look at") — 好 + [verb] forms an adjective meaning "good to [verb]," so 好笑 literally reads "good to laugh at."

examples.hanzi: 他学猫叫的样子真好笑。
examples.pinyin: Tā xué māo jiào de yàngzi zhēn hǎoxiào.
examples.english: The way he imitates a cat is really funny.

examples.hanzi: 这有什么好笑的?我是认真的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè yǒu shénme hǎoxiào de? Wǒ shì rènzhēn de.
examples.english: What's so funny about that? I'm serious.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.
氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.

example.hanzi: 关于这件事,大家有不同的说法。
example.pinyin: Guānyú zhè jiàn shì, dàjiā yǒu bùtóng de shuōfa.
example.english: Regarding this matter, everyone has a different version of events.
example.fact: CEDICT lists two distinct readings for the same two characters: the everyday shuō·fa (法 toneless) means "a way of putting things, a statement or version," while the fully-toned shuō fǎ is a much rarer Buddhist term meaning "to expound the Dharma" (讲经说法) — an easy trap for automated pinyin lookups, since only the tone on 法 tells the two apart.

examples.hanzi: 你这个说法我不同意。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhège shuōfa wǒ bù tóngyì.
examples.english: I don't agree with your claim.

examples.hanzi: 这是一种新的说法,以前没人这么讲。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yì zhǒng xīn de shuōfa, yǐqián méi rén zhème jiǎng.
examples.english: This is a new expression that no one used before.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.

example.hanzi: 他想借钱,却不知道怎么开口。
example.pinyin: Tā xiǎng jiè qián, què bù zhīdào zěnme kāikǒu.
example.english: He wants to borrow money, but doesn't know how to bring it up.
example.fact: 开口 extends past its literal sense "to open one's mouth" into "to broach a difficult or awkward topic," often paired with 难 to form 难以开口 ("hard to bring oneself to say") — capturing the hesitation before saying something uncomfortable.

examples.hanzi: 请你开口说一说你的想法。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ kāikǒu shuō yi shuō nǐ de xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: Please speak up and share your thoughts.

examples.hanzi: 他不好意思开口向朋友借钱。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù hǎoyìsi kāikǒu xiàng péngyou jiè qián.
examples.english: He felt shy about asking friends to lend him money.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.
阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — relates to hills, walls and places, as in 院 courtyard, 阳 sun-side, 陆 land; fits 际 as a boundary.
示 (shì) is only a loose sound hint — traditional 際 used 祭 (jì), and simplification swapped in 示.

example.hanzi: 这家公司正在拓展国际市场。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhèngzài tuòzhǎn guójì shìchǎng.
example.english: This company is expanding into international markets.
example.fact: 国际 functions only as an attributive modifier before a noun (国际市场, 国际关系) and never stands alone as "internationally" — for that adverbial sense Chinese instead uses 在国际上, a distinction easy to miss since English "international" can sit more loosely in a sentence.

examples.hanzi: 这是一个国际航班。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge guójì hángbān.
examples.english: This is an international flight.

examples.hanzi: 我们学校有很多国际学生。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xuéxiào yǒu hěn duō guójì xuésheng.
examples.english: Our school has a lot of international students.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 仪 is the conduct of a person, as in 仪式 ceremony.
义 (yì) — near sound — 仪 is yí; 义 also sounds out 议 yì.
弋 (yì) is a loose sound clue for shì; 弋 also in 试 shì and 拭 shì.
工 (work, craft) — a craftsman's pattern, a standard.

example.hanzi: 学校为新生举行了开学仪式。
example.pinyin: Xuéxiào wèi xīnshēng jǔxíng le kāixué yíshì.
example.english: The school held an opening ceremony for the new students.
example.fact: 式 (弋 "tool" + 工 "measuring square") originally meant a model or standard for making things to a fixed pattern — 仪式 extends that same "set pattern" from craftsmanship to the fixed sequence of actions and words expected on a formal occasion.

examples.hanzi: 毕业仪式在下午三点开始。
examples.pinyin: Bìyè yíshì zài xiàwǔ sān diǎn kāishǐ.
examples.english: The graduation ceremony starts at three in the afternoon.

examples.hanzi: 婚礼的仪式很简单,但是很感人。
examples.pinyin: Hūnlǐ de yíshì hěn jiǎndān, dànshì hěn gǎnrén.
examples.english: The wedding ceremony was simple but moving.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 投 is to throw.
殳 (shū) is a weapon-in-hand part that is only a loose sound clue; it also appears in 设 shè and 段 duàn.
入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.

example.hanzi: 公司投入了大量资金开发新产品。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī tóurù le dàliàng zījīn kāifā xīn chǎnpǐn.
example.english: The company invested a large amount of capital to develop new products.
example.fact: 投入 stretches from the literal "to throw into" (投 "to throw" + 入 "to enter") all the way to the abstract "to invest [money, effort]" and even the adjective "absorbed, engrossed" (他工作很投入, "he's very absorbed in his work") — the same image of throwing oneself in covers financial, emotional, and mental commitment alike.

examples.hanzi: 他全身心地投入到工作中。
examples.pinyin: Tā quán shēnxīn de tóurù dào gōngzuò zhōng.
examples.english: He threw himself fully into his work.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅明年要投入使用。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng míngnián yào tóurù shǐyòng.
examples.english: This restaurant will be put into use next year.

components.note: 成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.
灬 (fire) — 灬 is fire at the bottom, as in 热, 照, 点; 熟 is cooked food, then ripe and familiar.
孰 (shú) — same sound — 熟 is shú, like 孰.

example.hanzi: 这些苹果还没有完全成熟。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē píngguǒ hái méiyǒu wánquán chéngshú.
example.english: These apples aren't completely ripe yet.
example.fact: 熟 (灬 "fire" + phonetic 孰, an exact sound match) originally described food fully cooked over a flame — 成熟 extends that same "fully done, ready" image from cooked food to ripened fruit and, metaphorically, to a person's emotional or intellectual maturity.

examples.hanzi: 他才二十岁,但是想法已经很成熟了。
examples.pinyin: Tā cái èrshí suì, dànshì xiǎngfǎ yǐjīng hěn chéngshú le.
examples.english: He's only twenty but already thinks quite maturely.

examples.hanzi: 西瓜成熟了,可以摘了。
examples.pinyin: Xīguā chéngshú le, kěyǐ zhāi le.
examples.english: The watermelons are ripe and can be picked.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 爱; 恋 is to love or long for.
The sound part is traditional 戀 (luán), replaced in 恋 by 亦 (yì) only for simplicity — a loose clue for liàn.

example.hanzi: 他们谈恋爱已经三年了。
example.pinyin: Tāmen tán liàn'ài yǐjīng sān nián le.
example.english: They have been together for three years.
example.fact: 恋 sits mostly in compounds: 恋爱 (romantic love), 初恋 (first love), 失恋 (heartbreak), 恋人 (lover). 谈恋爱 literally 'to talk about romance' is the everyday way to say 'to be dating'. You say 我爱你, not 我恋你.

examples.hanzi: 他很恋家,不想去外地工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn liàn jiā, bù xiǎng qù wàidì gōngzuò.
examples.english: He's very attached to home and doesn't want to work elsewhere.

examples.hanzi: 她的初恋是在大学里。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chūliàn shì zài dàxué lǐ.
examples.english: Her first love was in college.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — planning is done by talking things through; also 议 discuss, 论 discuss.
某 (mǒu) is a near sound match for móu; same part in 媒 méi and 煤 méi.
乂 (to cut, crisscross) — old for mowing or cutting. Dictionary story: someone cut down 乂 and buried in a wooden coffin 木, a vivid memory aid.
木 (tree, wood) — the bottom. In 杀 it is a leftover of the old 殺 form rather than meaning wood; 殺 also had 殳 (weapon in hand).
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌, 树, 板: 案 is a wooden table.
安 (ān) is a close sound clue for àn; also in 按 àn.

example.hanzi: 警方正在调查这起谋杀案。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá zhè qǐ móushā'àn.
example.english: The police are investigating this murder case.
example.fact: 案 (木 "wood" + phonetic 安) originally named a wooden table or desk — the "case" sense in 谋杀案 grew out of documents and evidence being laid out on that desk for a judge to review, the same table-to-case extension behind the English phrase "the bench."

examples.hanzi: 这起谋杀案发生在去年冬天。
examples.pinyin: Zhè qǐ móushā'àn fāshēng zài qùnián dōngtiān.
examples.english: This murder case happened last winter.

examples.hanzi: 他喜欢读关于谋杀案的推理小说。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan dú guānyú móushā'àn de tuīlǐ xiǎoshuō.
examples.english: He likes reading mystery novels about murder cases.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and mixing liquids, as in 河, 海, 清: 混 is to mix or muddy.
昆 (kūn) is a close sound clue for hùn; 昆 also in 棍 gùn.
舌 (tongue) — the left part, as in 话 speech. Memory aid: too many wagging tongues create chaos, hence 混乱.
乚 (hook) — the right-hand stroke and dictionary radical. 乱 is simplified from 亂; the stroke does not add meaning.

example.hanzi: 交通事故导致了严重的交通混乱。
example.pinyin: Jiāotōng shìgù dǎozhì le yánzhòng de jiāotōng hùnluàn.
example.english: The traffic accident caused serious traffic chaos.
example.fact: 混 (氵 "water" + phonetic 昆) originally described muddy water where clean and dirty had mixed together indistinguishably — 混乱 keeps that same core image of things jumbled together without order, whether it's liquids, traffic, or a chaotic situation.

examples.hanzi: 他的房间里一片混乱,到处都是衣服。
examples.pinyin: Tā de fángjiān lǐ yí piàn hùnluàn, dàochù dōu shì yīfu.
examples.english: His room is a mess, with clothes everywhere.

examples.hanzi: 比赛结束后,场面一度很混乱。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài jiéshù hòu, chǎngmiàn yídù hěn hùnluàn.
examples.english: After the game ended, the scene was chaotic for a while.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 我对这次考试很有信心。
example.pinyin: Wǒ duì zhè cì kǎoshì hěn yǒu xìnxīn.
example.english: I'm very confident about this exam.
example.fact: 信心 almost always appears with 有 or 没有 (有信心 "to have confidence," 没信心 "to lack confidence") rather than as the subject of its own sentence — Chinese grammatically treats confidence as something you hold, not simply a state you are.

examples.hanzi: 你要对自己有信心。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào duì zìjǐ yǒu xìnxīn.
examples.english: You need to have confidence in yourself.

examples.hanzi: 这次失败让他失去了信心。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì shībài ràng tā shīqù le xìnxīn.
examples.english: This failure made him lose his confidence.

components.note: 當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).
成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.

example.hanzi: 他一直把我当成最好的朋友。
example.pinyin: Tā yìzhí bǎ wǒ dàngchéng zuì hǎo de péngyou.
example.english: He has always treated me as his best friend.
example.fact: 当成 almost always shows up inside a 把 construction (把 A 当成 B, "to treat A as B"), with the object A fronted before the verb — a word-order pattern with no direct equivalent in English's ordinary subject-verb-object structure.

examples.hanzi: 别把我的话当成耳边风。
examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ wǒ de huà dàngchéng ěrbiān fēng.
examples.english: Don't treat my words as if they were nothing.

examples.hanzi: 她把这里当成了自己的家。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhèlǐ dàngchéng le zìjǐ de jiā.
examples.english: She considers this place her own home.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 级 level; 经 first meant a warp thread, then "classics, pass through".
巠 (jīng), here simplified to look like 圣, gives the same sound; also in 茎 jīng, 径 jìng and 轻 qīng.

example.hanzi: 这条路经过我家。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù jīngguò wǒ jiā.
example.english: This road passes by my house.
example.fact: 经 originally meant the lengthwise threads of fabric, the warp; 纬 was the weft. That is why 经度 and 纬度 are longitude and latitude. The meaning grew to 'to pass through' (经过), 'to experience' (经验), and 'classic' (佛经, sutra).

examples.hanzi: 他经常在这家店买咖啡。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīngcháng zài zhè jiā diàn mǎi kāfēi.
examples.english: He often buys coffee at this shop.

examples.hanzi: 我已经吃过饭了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng chī guo fàn le.
examples.english: I have already eaten.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — marks feelings, as in 情, 怕, 悲; 惨 is a wretched, painful feeling.
参 (cān) gives the sound: 惨 cǎn is close, as in 掺 chān.

example.hanzi: 他输得很惨。
example.pinyin: Tā shū de hěn cǎn.
example.english: He lost badly.
example.fact: 惨 is often used after 得 to say something went terribly: 输得很惨 (lost badly). Colloquially 我惨了 means 'I'm doomed', and 太惨了 is an exclamation of sympathy. The related 悲惨 is a more formal tragic word.

examples.hanzi: 昨天的交通事故真惨。
examples.pinyin: Zuótiān de jiāotōng shìgù zhēn cǎn.
examples.english: Yesterday's traffic accident was terrible.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影的结局很悲惨。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng de jiéjú hěn bēicǎn.
examples.english: The ending of this film is very tragic.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — hearing and joining, as in 听, 聪, 闻: 联 first meant ears joined, so to link. The part 关 stands in for the traditional shape.
纟 (silk, thread) — 纟 is the simplified 糸 (thread), as in 红, 给; 络 is a net of threads, as in 网络.
各 (gè) — near sound — 络 is luò; 各 also sounds out 洛 luò and 路 lù.

example.hanzi: 请保持联络,有消息随时通知我。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎochí liánluò, yǒu xiāoxi suíshí tōngzhī wǒ.
example.english: Please stay in touch, let me know as soon as there's news.
example.fact: 络 (纟 "thread" + phonetic 各) pictures threads woven together into a net — 联络, pairing it with 联 ("linked, connected"), treats staying in contact as literally keeping a web of threads intact between people, much like English's own "network."

examples.hanzi: 你到了以后,请马上联络我。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ dào le yǐhòu, qǐng mǎshàng liánluò wǒ.
examples.english: After you arrive, please contact me right away.

examples.hanzi: 我们已经很久没有联络了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yǐjīng hěn jiǔ méiyǒu liánluò le.
examples.english: We haven't been in touch for a long time.
